# Renaissance Labs · Learn

> Films and lessons on how language models are trained and how human minds work. Free, sourced, in plain language.

## Course
- [What a language model actually is](https://learn.renaissancelabs.eu/lessons/what-is-a-language-model/): A language model is a function that predicts the next piece of text. Everything else, from chat to code, is built on top of that one trick.
- [Tokens: how text becomes numbers](https://learn.renaissancelabs.eu/lessons/tokens/): Models read and write tokens, not words. Tokens decide what you pay for, how much fits in context, and why models stumble on spelling and arithmetic.
- [Attention and the transformer](https://learn.renaissancelabs.eu/lessons/attention-and-the-transformer/): Attention lets each token look back at earlier tokens and decide which ones matter. Stacked many times, it is the core of every modern language model.
- [How a model learns](https://learn.renaissancelabs.eu/lessons/how-a-model-learns/): Training is a loop that measures how surprised the model was by real text and nudges its parameters to be less surprised next time.
- [Pretraining data](https://learn.renaissancelabs.eu/lessons/pretraining-data/): Frontier models read tens of trillions of tokens, but most of the raw web is thrown away first. Quality, mixture and repetition shape what the model learns.
- [Scaling laws: how big, how long](https://learn.renaissancelabs.eu/lessons/scaling-laws/): Loss falls smoothly as parameters, data and compute grow. Scaling laws turn that into a budgeting tool, and also show where the tool stops working.
- [Parameters, precision and memory](https://learn.renaissancelabs.eu/lessons/parameters-precision-and-memory/): A parameter is a stored number, and every number costs bytes. Precision, gradients and optimizer state decide whether a model fits on one chip or needs a cluster.
- [GPUs and parallelism](https://learn.renaissancelabs.eu/lessons/gpus-and-parallelism/): A GPU is fast only when its arithmetic units stay fed. Training a large model means splitting it across thousands of GPUs in several ways at once, and paying for the communication.
- [Mixture of experts](https://learn.renaissancelabs.eu/lessons/mixture-of-experts/): A mixture-of-experts model stores many specialist sub-networks but sends each token to only a few. It gets the capacity of a huge model at the arithmetic cost of a much smaller one.
- [When training breaks](https://learn.renaissancelabs.eu/lessons/when-training-breaks/): At frontier scale something is always failing. How labs survive broken chips, loss spikes, silent wrong answers and fragile low-precision numbers.
- [Supervised fine-tuning](https://learn.renaissancelabs.eu/lessons/supervised-fine-tuning/): How a raw text predictor becomes an assistant by studying examples of good answers, and why a small, clean dataset can beat a large, messy one.
- [Preference tuning and reinforcement learning](https://learn.renaissancelabs.eu/lessons/preference-tuning-and-rl/): How models learn from comparisons and from checkable rewards: RLHF, DPO, verifiable rewards, group-based RL, and the sandboxes and reward hacking that come with it.
- [Evaluation](https://learn.renaissancelabs.eu/lessons/evaluation/): How we measure what a model can do, and why every measurement has a catch: contamination, saturation, judge bias and scores that cannot be compared across versions.
- [Distillation and quantization](https://learn.renaissancelabs.eu/lessons/distillation-and-quantization/): Two ways to make a model cheaper to run: teach a small model to imitate a big one, or store the same weights in fewer bits. What each one keeps, and what it costs.
- [Inference and sampling](https://learn.renaissancelabs.eu/lessons/inference-and-sampling/): How a trained model produces text: a fast reading phase, a slow one-token-at-a-time writing phase, a memory called the KV cache, and the sampling rules that pick each token.
- [What "open" means for AI models](https://learn.renaissancelabs.eu/lessons/what-open-means/): "Open" can mean downloadable weights, public code, released data or a full training recipe. These are different things, with different freedoms, and few releases include all four.
- [How a base model is trained, end to end](https://learn.renaissancelabs.eu/lessons/base-training/): Every step from raw text to a base model, followed through one real model, the OpenEuroLLM 9B that sits under Agora, with interactive demos of the loss, the optimizer, the schedule and long context.
- [How a base model becomes an assistant, end to end](https://learn.renaissancelabs.eu/lessons/post-training/): Seven stages of post-training followed through one real model, Agora 9B, with its data, recipes, costs and scores, and interactive demos of loss masking, preference tuning, weight merging and reinforcement learning.

## Notes
- [Teaching a 9B model to say “I don't know”](https://learn.renaissancelabs.eu/notes/hallucination-and-i-dont-know/): A 9B model invented an answer for 98% of made-up names. Two short training stages cut that to 2%. What worked, what failed, and what the fix cost.
- [Models that decide: Jev, Kev and Sven, from a hosted API to Swedish authority cases](https://learn.renaissancelabs.eu/notes/decision-models-jev-kev-sven/): A decision model does not write text. It reads a case and answers typed questions with a probability. How the design works, how Kev made it open, and what two small Swedish derivatives learned and did not learn.
- [Who are you? How identity datasets teach a model about itself](https://learn.renaissancelabs.eu/notes/identity-datasets/): A model does not know its own name, who built it or when its data ends. Someone has to teach it. How identity data works, what goes wrong without it, and the OpenEuroLLM identity dataset as a worked example.
- [How models learned to prefer: RLHF, DPO and alignment, from ChatGPT to a European 9B](https://learn.renaissancelabs.eu/notes/preference-tuning-and-alignment/): A history of preference tuning from the first human-feedback experiments to DPO, and a close reading of one real checkpoint: what the data was, what moved, what did not, and what the benchmark can and cannot say.
- [In practice there is a difference](https://learn.renaissancelabs.eu/notes/theory-and-practice/): Running a job on a cluster is a skill of its own. Making something work before you understand why is a legitimate first step, as long as you come back for the why.

## Recipes
- [Full-weight DPO on 1.4 million preference pairs](https://learn.renaissancelabs.eu/recipes/oellm-9b-threeway-dpo/): Take a supervised fine-tuned 9B model and tune it on pairs of preferred and rejected answers. One epoch, every weight updated, 32 GPUs, under two days.
- [SFT warm start, then on-policy DPO, against hallucination](https://learn.renaissancelabs.eu/recipes/prelude-9b-hallucination-r2/): Take a 9B model that invents an answer for 98% of made-up names. Fine-tune it on honest answers for 12 minutes, then run a short DPO round on its own mistakes. Fabrication falls to 2%.

## Topics
- [Preference tuning](https://learn.renaissancelabs.eu/tags/preference-tuning/): Training on pairs of better and worse answers, with DPO and its relatives.
- [Multilingual](https://learn.renaissancelabs.eu/tags/multilingual/): Work across many languages, beyond English.
- [Supervised fine-tuning](https://learn.renaissancelabs.eu/tags/supervised-fine-tuning/): Teaching a model by showing it the answers you want.
- [Datasets](https://learn.renaissancelabs.eu/tags/datasets/): Building, checking and documenting training data.
- [Evaluation](https://learn.renaissancelabs.eu/tags/evaluation/): How to measure a model, and what the measurements miss.
- [Hallucination](https://learn.renaissancelabs.eu/tags/hallucination/): Models that make things up, and how to measure and train against it.
- [Training practice](https://learn.renaissancelabs.eu/tags/training-practice/): The craft of running training jobs, and what goes wrong.
- [Alignment](https://learn.renaissancelabs.eu/tags/alignment/): Getting a model to behave as intended.
- [Decision models](https://learn.renaissancelabs.eu/tags/decision-models/): Small models that answer typed questions in one pass.
- [Model identity](https://learn.renaissancelabs.eu/tags/identity/): What a model says about itself, and how it learns it.
- [Reinforcement learning](https://learn.renaissancelabs.eu/tags/reinforcement-learning/): Training on rewards for what the model does.
- [Swedish](https://learn.renaissancelabs.eu/tags/swedish/): Models and data for Swedish.

## Films
- [Keeping AI agents safe: injection, incidents and design](https://learn.renaissancelabs.eu/films/agent-safety/): Why agents raise the stakes over chatbots, how prompt injection works, real incidents, and the design rules and habits that limit the damage.
- [Post-training a European model, stage by stage](https://learn.renaissancelabs.eu/films/post-training/): A walkthrough of turning a raw 9-billion-parameter European base model into an assistant, with the bugs, evaluations and fixes found at each stage.
- [Envy is a compass](https://learn.renaissancelabs.eu/films/envy/): Envy is not proof that you are a bad friend. It is precise, and it points at what you still want.
- [The mind is a machine that makes up stories](https://learn.renaissancelabs.eu/films/mind-making-up-stories/): The mind turns what happens into stories about you and the world. Seeing them as stories makes room for other, more accurate ones.
- [What is intelligence?](https://learn.renaissancelabs.eu/films/intelligence/): A short essay in film: intelligence as finding and keeping the right pattern, and how brains and language models share that shape.
- [The alignment problem: whose values should AI follow?](https://learn.renaissancelabs.eu/films/alignment-problem/): How assistants learn behavior from human choices, four questions where reasonable people disagree, and the ways ordinary people can take part.
- [Why AI makes things up and how to guard against it](https://learn.renaissancelabs.eu/films/hallucinations/): Why language models state invented facts with confidence, how a model can learn to say it does not know, and what you can do to protect yourself.
- [Where the silicon ends](https://learn.renaissancelabs.eu/films/gpu-hardware/): Why Hopper cannot run 4-bit math at full speed and Blackwell can, and which GPU limits are carved in silicon rather than code.
- [How AI agents work: build one from scratch](https://learn.renaissancelabs.eu/films/how-agents-work/): Builds an agent piece by piece: a model that predicts text, a context list, tools, a loop, then memory, skills, sub-agents and autonomy.
- [Memory is an experience](https://learn.renaissancelabs.eu/films/memory/): Each time you remember, you rebuild the memory in the present, which means the way you see the past can change.
- [Running on empty: understanding burnout](https://learn.renaissancelabs.eu/films/burnout/): If you wake up already tired, you may not be lazy. Burnout has a shape that research describes, and five steps that help you come back.
- [How reinforcement learning scales for language models](https://learn.renaissancelabs.eu/films/rl-scaling/): How labs run reinforcement learning at production scale: the algorithms, the environments and rewards, the infrastructure and the failure modes.
- [Looking inside AI: the science of interpretability](https://learn.renaissancelabs.eu/films/interpretability/): How researchers look inside neural networks: superposition, sparse autoencoders, features, circuit tracing, and what this may mean for safety.
- [Understanding your attachment style](https://learn.renaissancelabs.eu/films/attachment-heal/): Why you spiral, withdraw or push people away, how each pattern grew, and how to practice something steadier and support someone you love.
- [What it takes to train a frontier model](https://learn.renaissancelabs.eu/films/frontier-training/): A tour of what goes into training a 2026 frontier model: data, scaling, chips, parallelism, failures, post-training and cost.
- [The only place experience happens](https://learn.renaissancelabs.eu/films/present/): What the present moment is, why minds wander, and what the evidence says about mindfulness and awe.
- [Inkling 2 Small: training in 4-bit](https://learn.renaissancelabs.eu/films/inkling/): A look at how Inkling 2 Small was trained in native 4-bit, what the run probably cost, and how a smaller team could climb to the same recipe.
- [You are not alone in here](https://learn.renaissancelabs.eu/films/not-alone/): We see our own inside and everyone else's outside. This film looks at why that makes us feel separate, and at small ways to feel connected again.
- [Hello, old friend: living with fear](https://learn.renaissancelabs.eu/films/old-friend/): Fear is an old companion trying to keep you safe. A gentle film about neither obeying it nor fighting it.
- [How to feel and still choose](https://learn.renaissancelabs.eu/films/emotion-regulation/): Emotional regulation is not feeling less. It is a skill, built mostly with other people, and five practices can strengthen it.
- [Entropy: order and surprise](https://learn.renaissancelabs.eu/films/entropy/): Shannon's entropy, followed through physics, the entropic brain hypothesis and the training loss of a language model.
- [Act first, and do what you say](https://learn.renaissancelabs.eu/films/act-first/): Motivation often follows action. A smaller, kinder way to close the gap between what you say you will do and what you do.
- [A simple model of how the mind processes information](https://learn.renaissancelabs.eu/films/how-the-mind-processes-information/): A simplified model of how senses, feelings and thoughts feed one another, and why changing your inner models can change how the world feels.
- [Inside the strongest open models](https://learn.renaissancelabs.eu/films/open-models/): Ten leading open-weights models compared: sparse experts, compressed attention, stability, data, and why post-training seems to decide the score.
- [Running AI agents safely on a cluster](https://learn.renaissancelabs.eu/films/cluster-agents/): How to let a learning agent use the real internet without letting it do real damage: sandboxes, egress proxies, logging and staged rollouts.
- [Make a Fool of Yourself](https://learn.renaissancelabs.eu/films/fool/): Why the fear of cringe feels so big, why it is often wrong, and a week of small, deliberate foolishness.
- [The future is a story you tell today](https://learn.renaissancelabs.eu/films/future/): How the brain builds the future from memory, where it goes wrong, and four gentle questions that make the story kinder.
